newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs strong but not seen rising further.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs strong but not seen rising further.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carriers (VLCCs) continued to hold their strength on Monday but some brokers said they did not expect the market to rise further in the next few days.
"The market's looking quite strong, especially to Korea and Japan, but I think it might be reaching a plateau.
"This could be a bit of a testing week...I think owners will be happy for the market to hold where it is," one broker said.

VLCCs to Japan and South Korea remained at their year high of about W75, as witnessed by the 250,000 tonne Shoju Maru fixed at W76.5 to Japan for SSS and the 260,000 tonne Hyundai Star, done at W74.5 to South Korea for Yukong.
Even for a shorter voyage to Singapore, W75 was achieved by the 250,000 tonne Eleuthera for Sietco.
VLCCs from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf were quiet, remaining at around W65, while million-barrel (130,000 tonne) vessels were seen softening from their recent W95 on a lack of enquiry, brokers said.
In the transatlantic sector, the 290,000 tonne Berge Nisa was heard done North Sea/USG at W70 for Shell.
The Mediterranean market was quiet, with a handful of 80,000 tonne vessels fixed in the current range of W107.5-112.5 and million-tonne ships still assessed around W95.
The inter-U.K./Cont market was moribund with little if any business done since Friday when the last vessel was done at W90, brokers said.
Fuel oil was steady, with 25,000 tonnes inter-UKC at W250/260 and cross-Med at W190/195.

The Caribbean market was little changed with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes at W212.5-215 and 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems at W200. "Those markets are maintaining their activity," a U.S. broker said. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
